title: Jobs carry an estimated cost from a configurable rate card
description:
Turn billed seconds into dollars, and store the result on the job so cost is
attributable per clip, per site, and per backend without recomputation.

Two cost components, always reported separately:

- **GPU cost** -- `billed_seconds x hourly_rate / 3600`. Zero for local jobs.
- **Platform cost** -- DynamoDB, Lambda, S3 storage, CloudFront egress. Small
  per job but never zero, and charged for local jobs too.

A console that prints "$0.00" for a locally processed job states something
false. Local synthesis avoids the GPU line, not the platform line.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Estimated cost per job

  Scenario: A Batch job is costed from its billed seconds
    Given the GPU rate is 0.526 dollars per hour
    And a Batch job recorded 3600 billed seconds
    When the job cost is calculated
    Then the job gpu cost is 0.526 dollars

  Scenario: A locally processed job has no GPU cost
    Given a job was claimed by a local worker
    When the job cost is calculated
    Then the job gpu cost is zero
    And the job platform cost is greater than zero

  Scenario: A job records the rate card it was costed against
    Given the GPU rate is 0.526 dollars per hour
    When the job cost is calculated
    Then the job records the rate and the rate card version

  Scenario: Changing the rate card does not restate historical jobs
    Given a job was costed at 0.526 dollars per hour
    When the rate card is changed to 0.40 dollars per hour
    Then the existing job still records 0.526 dollars per hour

  Scenario: A failed Batch job is still costed
    Given a Batch job failed after 600 billed seconds
    When the job cost is calculated
    Then the job gpu cost is greater than zero
```

Historical jobs must not be silently restated when the rate card changes --
a cost report that changes retroactively is not a cost report. Stamp the rate
onto the record at calculation time.

## Implementation brief

**Rate card** -- CDK context, surfaced to Lambdas as environment variables:

- `gpu_hourly_rate_usd` -- default for `g4dn.xlarge` on-demand in us-east-1.
  **Verify the current published price at implementation time rather than
  trusting a constant in this description**; it is roughly 0.526 but that is
  from memory, region-specific, and subject to change.
- `platform_cost_per_job_usd` -- a flat modelled allowance. Deriving true
  per-job DynamoDB/Lambda/S3/CloudFront cost is not worth the complexity; a
  flat estimate the reconciliation story can calibrate is honest and cheap.
- `rate_card_version` -- a string stamped onto every costed job.

**`cdk/lambdas/batch_telemetry/handler.py`** -- calculate and write
`gpu_cost_usd`, `platform_cost_usd`, `cost_rate_usd_per_hour`,
`rate_card_version` when billed seconds are recorded.

**`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py`** -- `_mark_done` and `_mark_failed` write
`gpu_cost_usd = 0` and the platform cost for local jobs. Batch jobs get their
GPU cost from the telemetry Lambda, which may arrive after `_mark_done`; the
two writes must not clobber each other. Use separate attributes and distinct
`update_item` calls, not a read-modify-write of a single cost blob.

**Store costs as DynamoDB `Decimal`**, never float. `_json_default` already
converts `Decimal` for responses. Fractions of a cent accumulated across
thousands of jobs in binary floating point will not sum correctly, and this
is money.

**`docs/`** -- document the methodology: what is estimated, what is measured,
what the platform allowance covers, and that these are modelled figures rather
than invoice lines. Anyone reading a dollar figure in the console needs to
know which it is.

## Blocked on

The Batch billing telemetry story, which supplies `billed_seconds`.

comments.text: Implemented on feature/job-cost-estimate, merged to develop. _mark_done/_mark_failed now write gpu_cost_usd (0, overwritten by batch_telemetry for Batch jobs), platform_cost_usd (flat allowance, every job), cost_rate_usd_per_hour, and rate_card_version, via extended (not replaced) UpdateExpressions so neither writer clobbers the other. batch_telemetry independently computes and writes the real gpu_cost_usd/rate/version for Batch jobs in pure Decimal arithmetic, self-consistent regardless of write order versus mark_done (documented as a known ordering limitation, not a false guarantee). GPU rate defaulted to $0.526/hr for g4dn.xlarge on-demand us-east-1, sourced from two independent third-party pricing aggregators (moderate confidence, not confirmed against AWS's own pricing API or a real invoice -- documented plainly in code, override via gpu_hourly_rate_usd context). Platform allowance ($0.0005/job) explicitly labelled as an unmeasured placeholder. auritus job show now surfaces all four cost fields. Independently re-verified: reverted the router changes myself and confirmed all 3 scenarios genuinely fail (tied to the actual cost fields, not a bare status code). Full suite green: black/ruff, cli pytest (59 passed), behave (28 features, 106 scenarios), cdk pytest (33 passed), cdk synth clean.
